transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um... well, I guess I'm just here because I... I can't really seem to stop worrying. It's just... everything at once, lately. 

Work stuff—like if my performance is slipping. Bills. These house projects I keep dropping. And, um... my marriage. Just... wondering if I'm basically failing as a husband. And a dad. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been affecting your ability to function in your daily life—like at work, home, or with family?

Um... probably about nine months. Give or take. 

That's, uh... that's when this big cloud migration project ramped up at work. And... I guess that's also around the time the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing. 

So... yeah. It makes things difficult.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or stomach issues, that seem to come along with your worrying?

Um... yeah, I guess sleep is an issue. 

I'll be exhausted when I get into bed, but... I just lie there. My brain keeps running through, you know, work risks... money... stuff I said to my wife. 

And, uh... even if I do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up around 3 or 4. I can't get back down after that. I just lie there... already rehearsing tomorrow's problems, I guess.
Do you find that you feel anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific reason for it?

Um... yeah. Most days, I guess. 

It doesn't really seem to matter if something is actually happening or not. It's just... kind of always there in the background. 

So... yeah.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can't control, even when you try to stop thinking about these things?

Um... yeah. It's hard. 

I try to stop. I'll tell myself to just... focus on the code in front of me, or... try to just breathe through a workout. But... it doesn't really work. 

One concern just sort of... hooks another. Before I know it, I'm twenty steps ahead. I'll be imagining getting a bad review, which turns into... losing my job. And then my family being worse off, all because of me. 

So... yeah. I can't really stop it.
Would you say that your anxiety or worrying happens on most days, rather than just occasionally?
Um... yeah. Like I just said, it's... most days. It's not just every once in a while.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with your family?

Um... no, not really. 

I mean, I still go to the gym. I still see my wife and kids. I don't feel... hopeless, exactly. Just... always on edge, I guess. But I still do the things I normally do.
Have you found yourself getting more irritable or restless lately, maybe more than usual for you?

Um... yeah, I guess. 

I'm just... wound pretty tight. Almost all day. It's like my shoulders are just... locked up. Like I'm bracing for something to happen. 

And... sitting still is hard. I end up pacing a lot between meetings. Or, um... if I'm at chess club, I'll just be tapping the pieces. I just... I can't really stay still.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks because of your anxiety or worrying?

Yeah. Work has been... difficult. 

Like, if I'm in sprint planning, or... doing code reviews. I'll end up reading the same design note three, maybe four times. And I still miss details. 

It's just... part of my head is always somewhere else. Like I'm stuck calculating what I forgot to do at home, or... thinking about how badly the next argument is gonna go. So, yeah. Staying focused is... not great right now.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes, along with physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?
No, I don't think so. I mean, my heart beats fast sometimes, but... not like an attack or anything. Just the usual stress.

Do you think your anxiety started in response to a specific event or situation, like the stress at work or the arguments at home, and do you feel like it should have improved by now if things had gone back to normal?

I don't know. Maybe. 

I guess work has been stressful for a while. And the stuff at home... it's just always there. 

But I'm not sure if it started because of one specific thing. It just feels like it's been this way for... a long time. I don't really know when it would have gotten better.
Do you feel that your level of anxiety is in line with the actual stress you’re experiencing, or does it sometimes feel like it's more intense or lasting longer than the situation seems to warrant?

I don't know. It's... hard to gauge, I guess. 

I haven't really thought about it like that. It just feels like a lot, pretty much all the time. I don't really know what the normal amount of worry is supposed to look like for this stuff. So... I'm not sure.
Do you find that your anxiety and worrying tend to jump around to different things, like work, family, health, or other everyday issues, rather than staying focused on just one specific problem?

Yeah... I guess so. That's kind of why I came in, honestly. I just can't stop worrying about... everything at once. 

It's not just one problem. It's my marriage, and... whether I'm slipping at work. Then the bills. Or these house projects I keep dropping. It just feels like... I don't know. Like I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. So, yeah. It jumps around a lot.
Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or worried even during times when there isn’t anything specific going on at work or at home to cause it?

I don't really know. 

I guess... maybe? It's hard to tell when nothing is going on. There's usually always something. But... yeah, I suppose even if it's quiet, I'm still just... waiting for the next thing to go wrong.
Would you say your anxiety and worrying have caused you significant distress or made it hard to carry out your normal responsibilities at work, home, or in your relationships?

Yeah, I guess it has. 

At work... my manager started documenting some architectural details I've been missing. So that's not great. And at home... I just leave things half-finished. I'm so distracted that... well, the arguments with my wife just keep getting worse. So... yeah, it's definitely making things hard.
Can you recall any days where nothing particularly stressful was happening at work or at home, and yet you still felt anxious or worried anyway?
I don't really know. Like I said... it's hard to tell. I don't really keep track of days like that.
Would you say that on most days, you feel anxious or worried, even if there isn’t a specific reason for it at that moment?
I guess... yeah. Probably most days. It's just... kind of always there in the background. I don't really know how else to explain it.
